st.headline: Sembcorp lifts interim dividend to 11 cents on stronger second-half outlook
st.teaser: The company's interim dividend for the first half of 2026 will be 11 cents per share.
fullText: SINGAPORE - Sembcorp Industries announced on Aug 13 a higher interim divide nd of 11 cents per share for the first half of 2026 – up from nine cents per share a year ago – as it expects stronger financial results for the second half.
This reflects confidence in the company’s future performance, it said in a Singapore Exchange filing before trading hours.
Sembcorp also expects more contributions from Australian energy supplier Alinta Energy, which it acquired in June.

This is even as the Singapore energy and urban solutions provider saw its underlying net profit fall 25 per cent to $369 million for the first half of 2026, compared with $491 million in the first half of 2025.
When taking in one-off acquisition costs, net profit fell by a larger margin of 72 per cent. Sembcorp had incurred a $155 million one-off transaction cost for the acquisition of Alinta.
Underlying net profit for Sembcorp’s three segments – gas and related services, renewables, and integrated urban solutions – also declined.
However, the company said if the Alinta acquisition had been completed in January instead of June 2026, net profit would have been $558 million, taking in six months of Alinta’s contributions.
Sembcorp group chief executive Wong Kim Yin said: “Alinta has performed better than expected in the first half of 2026.

“Looking ahead, we expect a stronger second-half performance, supported by the resilience of our diversified portfolio, contributions from Alinta and improved earnings prospects for our Singapore business.”
He added that as an integrated energy player, Sembcorp is well-positioned to capture structural demand growth from data centres and AI-related infrastructure.
“Our interim dividend of 11 cents per share, up 22 per cent from last year, reflects our confidence in the group’s future performance and our commitment to sustainable shareholder returns,” he said.
Sembcorp expects stronger earnings for the gas and related services segment in the second half.
This is supported by the commissioning of a 600-megawatt hydrogen-ready power plant, among other factors.
Sembcorp said in its results presentation: “The segment remains well-positioned to capture growing power demand in Singapore, particularly from data centre and high-tech manufacturing sectors.”
It added that Alinta is expected to strengthen the group’s earnings base and contribute to recurring cash flows over time.
Meanwhile, the integrated urban solutions segment is also projected to do better in the secon d half, driven by higher land sales.
“The business continues to make steady progress in developing 0.9 million sq m of ready-built factories, which are expected to contribute to recurring income upon completion,” Sembcorp said.
However, the renewables segment is expected to bring in lower earnings for the second half of 2026, driven by seasonal and tariff-related challenges.
Sembcorp said it expects lower resources and tariffs in China, partially offset by contribution from new operational capacity in India.
But overall, Sembcorp still expects its second-half underlying net profit to exceed that of the first half of 2026.
Sembcorp shares slid nearly 3 per cent to $5.56 at around 10am on Aug 13.

cna.headline: Starbucks Korea swings to Q2 operating loss after marketing backlash
cna.teaser: Starbucks Korea swings to Q2 operating loss after marketing backlash
fullText: SEOUL, Aug 13 : The operator of Starbucks Korea posted an operating loss in the second quarter as sales fell after backlash over a marketing campaign that evoked a brutal 1980 military crackdown on pro-democracy protesters, and the suspension of its flagship summer promotion.

• Starbucks Korea's operator SCK Company swung to an 18.4 billion won ($13.4 million) operating loss in the second quarter from an operating profit of 40.3 billion won a year earlier and 29.3 billion won in the preceding quarter.
• E-Mart, the parent of SCK, said in an earnings announcement on Thursday that SCK did not hold its usual summer promotional campaign in June.

• Parent Shinsegae Group dismissed the head of Starbucks Korea, while the group later said sales had dropped "very significantly" and held historical awareness and social sensitivity training for staff.
• On Thursday, E-Mart did not cite the controversy or subsequent boycott calls as a direct reason for the quarterly decline.

listening.title: Singapore's High-Tech Farming Shift
listening.transcript: Singapore’s coastal waters are seeing a technological upgrade as local fish farms adopt smart sensors and automated feeding systems. While traditional farmers face high operational costs, these high-tech solutions hope to make sustainable aquaculture commercially profitable for the long term.

economistArticle.title: Hooray for index funds—just don’t call them passive
paras: For decades, index-tracking funds have been heralded as the ultimate "passive" investment tool. By simply copying the composition of an index like the S&P 500, these financial vehicles offer low costs and steady, market-matching returns, effectively democratizing wealth creation for millions of ordinary savers. Jack Bogle’s brainchild, Vanguard, popularized this concept, convincing generations that trying to beat the market was a fool's errand.

However, calling these funds "passive" is a misnomer that masks the immense discretionary power held by index creators and fund managers. Index construction itself is a series of highly active, qualitative choices. Deciding which companies qualify for an index, how they are weighted, and when they are reconstituted involves human judgment, committees, and arbitrary thresholds. When a tech giant is reclassified or a failing giant is ejected, billions of dollars shift in an instant, dictated not by natural market forces but by index rulebooks.

Moreover, the rapid proliferation of customized and thematic indices has shattered the illusion of a neutral market. Today, investors can choose from indices targeting green energy, cybersecurity, or specific geographical regions. Selecting which index to track is, in itself, an active and often speculative bet. Rather than quietly riding the market tide, investors are actively curating their portfolios, using index funds as building blocks to express highly specific economic views.

The corporate governance implications of so-called passive investing are equally profound. The "Big Three" asset managers—BlackRock, Vanguard, and State Street—now control massive voting blocks in almost every major listed company. Far from being passive bystanders, these institutions engage in intensive dialogue with corporate boards, voting on everything from executive compensation to climate transition plans. Their decisions wield extraordinary influence over corporate behavior and capital allocation globally.

Ultimately, the rise of index investing represents a shift in where active decisions are made, rather than their elimination. The simplicity of buying a single fund obscures a vast infrastructure of strategic choices, market-moving index rebalances, and corporate stewardship. To celebrate the democratizing power of low-cost funds is entirely justified, but we must retire the myth of passivity.
economistArticle.cn:
几十年来，指数跟踪基金一直被誉为终极的“被动”投资工具。通过简单地复制标准普尔500指数等指数的构成，这些金融工具提供了低成本和稳定的、与市场相匹配的回报，有效地为数百万普通储蓄者实现了财富创造的民主化。杰克·博格尔的创意——先锋集团——推广了这一理念，让几代人相信，试图击败市场是徒劳的。
然而，将这些基金称为“被动”是一个误导性的名称，它掩盖了指数制定者和基金经理所拥有的巨大自由裁量权。指数构建本身就是一系列高度主动的、定性的选择。决定哪些公司有资格加入指数、它们如何加权以及何时进行重组，涉及人类的判断、委员会和任意设定的门槛。当一家科技巨头被重新分类，或一家衰落的巨头被剔除时，数百亿美元会在瞬间发生转移，这并非由自然的市场力量决定，而是由指数规则手册所主导。
此外，定制和主题指数的迅速泛滥，打破了中性市场的幻想。今天，投资者可以选择针对绿色能源、网络安全或特定地理区域的指数。选择跟踪哪个指数本身就是一种主动的、往往是投机性的押注。投资者并不是在静静地顺应市场潮流，而是正在积极地构建他们的投资组合，利用指数基金作为构建模块来表达高度特定的经济观点。
所谓被动投资对公司治理的影响也同样深远。三大资产管理公司——贝莱德、先锋和道富——现在几乎在每家大型上市公司中都控制着庞大的表决权。这些机构远非被动的旁观者，而是与公司董事会进行深入对话，对从高管薪酬到气候转型计划等所有事务进行投票。他们的决策对全球的企业行为和资本配置具有非凡的影响力。
归根结底，指数投资的兴起代表了主动决策发生地点的转移，而不是决策的消除。购买单一基金的简单性掩盖了战略选择、影响市场的指数重新平衡以及公司治理的庞大基础设施。庆祝低成本基金的民主化力量是完全有道理的，但我们必须摒弃被动性的神话。

gems.s: Deciding which companies qualify for an index, how they are weighted, and when they are reconstituted involves human judgment, committees, and arbitrary thresholds.
gems.why: This sentence uses parallel structures ('Deciding which...', 'how they...', 'and when they...') followed by a triad ('human judgment, committees, and arbitrary thresholds') to build a compelling and logically tight argument. 句子使用了并列结构和排比词组，使论点结构严密，说服力极强。

gems.s: To celebrate the democratizing power of low-cost funds is entirely justified, but we must retire the myth of passivity.
gems.why: This sentence employs a balanced contrast using the 'To do... is justified, but we must...' structure, effectively validating the opponent's view before delivering a sharp counterargument. 句子采用了平衡对比句式，在肯定对方观点的同时，迅速抛出犀利的反驳，极具说服力。
